main.title: Prince of Persia (2008)
main.subtitle: Trust Becomes a Movement
main.summary: Ubisoft Montreal begins a new Prince of Persia story with Elika, whose assistance shapes traversal, combat and recovery from falls.

cards.heading: A new journey with Elika
cards.text: Ubisoft Montreal released a new Prince of Persia for PlayStation 3 and Xbox 360 in December 2008. Separate from the Sands of Time trilogy, it follows a different protagonist travelling with Elika across a corrupted world. She extends jumps, assists in combat and rescues the Prince from falls, giving the partnership a role in nearly every part of play.

cards.heading: An illustrated landscape
cards.text: Dark outlines and painted surfaces give the characters and landscapes an illustrated appearance. The style keeps climbing routes visible while distinguishing areas affected by Corruption from places restored to life. Purification changes the colour and atmosphere of familiar spaces as the journey advances.

cards.heading: Elika's helping hand
cards.text: Elika can extend a jump, join an attack and activate powers associated with magical platforms. If the Prince falls, she returns him to a safe point so the attempt can resume quickly. Repeatedly calling on her assistance makes cooperation part of moving through the world as well as part of the story.

cards.heading: Restoring the regions
cards.text: The regions form an interconnected network that offers some freedom in the order of exploration. After a main confrontation, Elika purifies the area and the player revisits a brighter landscape. Combat focuses on one-on-one duels, keeping both characters involved while leaving exploration and acrobatics central to the adventure.

main.title: Dissidia Final Fantasy
main.summary: Dissidia Final Fantasy is a 2008 fighting game developed and published by Square Enix for the PlayStation Portable. It was released in Japan on December 18, 2008, in North America on August 25, 2009, and in Australia and Europe in September, as part of the campaign for the Final Fantasy series's 20th anniversary. It was then re-released in Japan, based on the North American version, as Dissidia Final Fantasy: Universal Tuning, on November 1, 2009.

cards.heading: Cosmos and Chaos summon Final Fantasy's champions
cards.text:
Dissidia Final Fantasy is a 2008 fighting game developed and published by Square Enix for the PlayStation Portable. It was released in Japan on December 18, 2008, in North America on August 25, 2009, and in Australia and Europe in September, as part of the campaign for the Final Fantasy series's 20th anniversary. It was then re-released in Japan, based on the North American version, as Dissidia Final Fantasy: Universal Tuning, on November 1, 2009.

The game features characters from different Final Fantasy games and centers on a great conflict between Cosmos, the goddess of harmony, and Chaos, the god of discord. The two summon multiple warriors to fight for their sides in their thirteenth war. During the story, the player controls the ten warriors chosen by Cosmos, the protagonists from the first ten Final Fantasy games, in their journey. The game's English and international versions give access to other features such as an arcade mode.

cards.heading: Three-dimensional arenas turn movement into combat
cards.text:
Dissidia Final Fantasy's genre has been described as "dramatic progressive action" and its graphics are in 3D. It has wireless one-on-one multiplayer and fights revolving around the use of individual special skills of characters to do damage to opponents. Players can customize their characters with equipment.

Character movement is fully functional within the three-dimensional field map. Characters are able to perform special maneuvers using the environment. Traps with a variety of ill effects can be found throughout the arena. Characters' equipment can be customized, and they can gain EXP and gil from battles.

cards.heading: Bravery becomes damage
cards.text: Bravery attacks steal an opponent's BRV and add it to the attacker's total. An HP attack then converts the accumulated Bravery into damage, after which the attacker's BRV drops to zero and gradually recovers. Driving an opponent's Bravery below zero causes a Break and awards the shared Bravery Pool to the attacker. The player must decide when to build more attack strength and when to spend it on reducing health.

cards.heading: Nomura turns a Kingdom Hearts idea into a Final Fantasy crossover
cards.text: Tetsuya Nomura first considered a Kingdom Hearts spin-off in which Disney characters fought one another, then shifted the concept towards Final Fantasy. Takeshi Arakawa directed the PSP crossover for the series' twentieth anniversary. Development took three years, with two devoted to the battle system and one to the role-playing mode. Wireless local matches were included, while the proposed online mode was left out.

cards.heading: Takeharu Ishimoto reworks the series' music
cards.text:
The Dissidia Final Fantasy Original Soundtrack by Takeharu Ishimoto was released on December 24, 2008, and is available in both regular and special editions, similar to the game itself. Most tracks are often remixes done by Ishimoto of past Final Fantasy music originally composed by Nobuo Uematsu.

The main theme of the game is "The Messenger" by Your Favorite Enemies. The tracks "Cosmos" and "Chaos - Last Battle 1" are also performed by Your Favorite Enemies. "The Messenger" is the main theme song of the game, with lyrics from both "Cosmos" and "Chaos - Last Battle 1". "Cosmos" features female vocals, while "Chaos" is dominated by male vocals. In YFE's documentary on the conception of the songs for Dissidia, lyricist-vocalist Alex Foster admitted that the lyrics have no direct connection to themes of the game; rather, he left it up to the listeners to interpret the lyrics based on their thoughts and ideas.

main.title: Spelunky
main.summary: Spelunky is a 2008 platform video game created by independent developer Derek Yu and released as source-available freeware for Microsoft Windows.

cards.heading: Every expedition enters different caves
cards.text: Spelunky is a 2008 platform video game created by independent developer Derek Yu and released as source-available freeware for Microsoft Windows. It was remade for the Xbox 360 in 2012, with ports of the new version following for various platforms, including back to Microsoft Windows. The player controls a spelunker who explores a series of caves while collecting treasure, saving damsels, fighting enemies, and dodging traps. The caves are procedurally generated, making each run-through of the game unique.

cards.heading: A freeware game becomes a remake
cards.text: The first public release was on December 21, 2008. The source code of the Windows version was released on December 25, 2009. An enhanced version for Xbox Live Arcade was released on July 4, 2012. The enhanced version was later released for Windows and PlayStation 3 in August 2013, and for PlayStation 4 in October 2014. The remake was also made available on Xbox One via backward compatibility in December 2015. A fanmade, ChromeOS version of the original game was made as well, titled Spelunky HTML5. A port for Nintendo Switch was released on August 26, 2021. A sequel, Spelunky 2, was released in September 2020.

cards.heading: Platforming meets the logic of roguelikes
cards.text: Spelunky was one of the first games to borrow concepts from roguelikes and combine them with real-time side-scrolling platformer elements. Due to its popularity, it was the influence for many later "roguelite" games. Spelunky received critical acclaim for its gameplay, atmosphere and design, though some controls and multiplayer elements polarized critics. Many critics and publications regarded it as one of the greatest video games of all time.

main.title: Demon's Souls
main.summary: Demon's Souls is a 2009 action role-playing game developed by FromSoftware and published by Sony Computer Entertainment for the PlayStation 3.

cards.heading: FromSoftware returns to dark fantasy
cards.text: Demon's Souls is a 2009 action role-playing game developed by FromSoftware and published by Sony Computer Entertainment for the PlayStation 3. It was released in Japan in February 2009, in North America by Atlus in October 2009, and in PAL territories by Namco Bandai Partners in June 2010. The game is referred to as a spiritual successor to FromSoftware's King's Field series.

cards.heading: Boletaria and the Nexus
cards.text: Demon's Souls is set in Boletaria, a kingdom consumed by a dark being called the Old One, following its release through the use of forbidden Soul Arts. Players take on the role of a hero brought to Boletaria to kill its fallen king Allant and pacify the Old One. Gameplay has players navigating five different worlds from a hub called the Nexus, with a heavy emphasis on challenging combat and mechanics surrounding player death and respawning. Online multiplayer allows both player cooperation and world invasions featuring player versus player combat.

cards.heading: Miyazaki takes over the project
cards.text: A collaboration between FromSoftware and Sony's Japan Studio, the game's early development was troubled due to a lack of coherent vision. Despite such issues, designer Hidetaka Miyazaki was able to take over the project and helped to turn the game into what it eventually became. The game's difficulty was intended to both evoke classic video games and provide a sense of challenge and accomplishment for players. This aspect proved demanding for Miyazaki, partly because of his fear that Sony would ask the team to lower the difficulty in order to make the game more accessible.

cards.heading: Word of mouth and a lasting influence
cards.text: Announced in 2008, early reactions to the Demon's Souls demo were seen as negative, and the game's high difficulty prompted Sony to pass on publishing the game outside of Japan. The game initially had slow sales in Japan, but achieved commercial and critical success in the West through positive word of mouth, exceeding sales expectations. It was praised for its difficult combat and addictive gameplay, subsequently winning several awards. Demon's Souls introduced many of the core elements that would define the Soulslike genre and it has since been cited as one of the greatest games of all time. Its success led to the spiritual successor series Dark Souls. FromSoftware's relationship with Sony would lead to the release of Bloodborne and Déraciné, while a remake of the same name was released in 2020 for the PlayStation 5.

main.title: Mario & Luigi: Bowser's Inside Story
main.subtitle: An adventure inside the enemy
main.summary: Mario & Luigi: Bowser's Inside Story is AlphaDream's Nintendo DS role-playing game that makes Bowser both a protagonist and a place to explore. After inhaling Mario and Luigi, he travels through the Mushroom Kingdom while the brothers investigate the world inside his body. Fawful's takeover gives them a common enemy, although Bowser does not understand who is helping him. The two scales of the adventure continually affect one another. An obstacle in the outside world can become a task for the much smaller travellers within.

cards.heading: An adventure inside the enemy
cards.text: Mario & Luigi: Bowser's Inside Story is AlphaDream's Nintendo DS role-playing game that makes Bowser both a protagonist and a place to explore. After inhaling Mario and Luigi, he travels through the Mushroom Kingdom while the brothers investigate the world inside his body. Fawful's takeover gives them a common enemy, although Bowser does not understand who is helping him. The two scales of the adventure continually affect one another. An obstacle in the outside world can become a task for the much smaller travellers within.

cards.heading: A punch above, a jump below
cards.text: Bowser explores an overhead world and fights with punches, fire and inhaling attacks. Mario and Luigi travel through side-on spaces inside him, using their familiar timed jumps, hammers and coordinated techniques. The DS screens distinguish these viewpoints, with different buttons assigned to the brothers and their enormous host. Enemies inhaled during Bowser's battles can even become opponents for Mario and Luigi. The arrangement makes the hardware's separation useful to the fiction: two related fights can occupy different parts of the same character at the same time.

cards.heading: Keep the body moving
cards.text: Some sections ask the brothers to stimulate Bowser's muscles or help him digest what he has eaten. Their small actions change what he can accomplish outside, turning a comic premise into a chain of practical cooperation. New abilities and special attacks provide more ways for both sides to progress. The player alternates between helping Bowser and using the result of that help, so neither viewpoint is merely an interruption. AlphaDream finds an unusually complete role for its unlikely lead: his personality drives the story, while his body supplies its structure.

main.title: Flower
main.summary: Flower is a video game developed by Thatgamecompany and published by Sony Computer Entertainment for the PlayStation 3.

cards.heading: Guiding the wind through a changing landscape
cards.text: Flower is Thatgamecompany's 2009 game about guiding the wind. Tilting the controller carries a petal through the air; brushing close to flowers adds more petals to the trail. These encounters also change the landscape, restoring colour to fields or setting wind turbines in motion. Designed by Jenova Chen and Nicholas Clark for PlayStation 3, it develops its story through movement, images and sound rather than dialogue. Later versions brought the same journey to other PlayStation systems, mobile devices and Windows.

cards.heading: Designing for an emotional response
cards.text: Flower was primarily intended to arouse positive emotions in the player, rather than to be a challenging and "fun" game. This focus was sparked by Chen, who felt that the primary purpose of entertainment products like video games was the feelings that they evoked in the audience and that the emotional range of most games was very limited. The team viewed their efforts as creating a work of art, removing gameplay elements and mechanics that were not provoking the desired response in the players. The music, composed by Vincent Diamante, dynamically responds to the player's actions and corresponds with the emotional cues in the game. Flower was a critical success, to the surprise of the developers. Reviewers praised the game's music, visuals, and gameplay, calling it a unique and compelling emotional experience. It was named the "best independent game of 2009" at the Spike Video Game Awards, and won the "Casual Game of the Year" award by the Academy of Interactive Arts and Sciences.

main.title: Killzone 2
main.subtitle: The invasion meets resistance in Helghan's streets
main.summary: Killzone 2 follows an ISA invasion of Helghan, placing the player in the boots of Sergeant Tomas Sevchenko. Guerrilla Games' PlayStation 3 shooter reached North American stores on 27 February 2009. Sev and his squad fight toward the capital through streets and industrial sites, facing an enemy defending its own territory under the rule of Scolar Visari.

cards.heading: Landing on Helghan
cards.text: Killzone 2 follows an ISA invasion of Helghan, placing the player in the boots of Sergeant Tomas Sevchenko. Guerrilla Games' PlayStation 3 shooter reached North American stores on 27 February 2009. Sev and his squad fight toward the capital through streets and industrial sites, facing an enemy defending its own territory under the rule of Scolar Visari.

cards.heading: Fighting from the edge of cover
cards.text: In the campaign, cover is something the player can work around from the first-person view. Leaning out to fire exposes a small part of the position, while staying still leaves time for enemies to advance or throw a grenade. Reloading and moving the weapon take a noticeable moment. These details make the exchange depend on choosing when to commit: a clear shot may be followed by the need to retreat behind the same piece of protection.

cards.heading: A hostile industrial world
cards.text: Helghan's machinery and military architecture give encounters their shape. Narrow approaches open onto yards or streets crossed by fire, and elevated positions can make a short advance difficult. Smoke, sparks and harsh lighting keep the industrial setting present even when attention is fixed on a target. The squad's movement gives the player a route through this confusion, but the opposition repeatedly interrupts that advance. Reaching the next position becomes a sequence of local decisions about shelter, visibility and timing.

cards.heading: One map, changing orders
cards.text: At release, online Warzone matches kept teams on the same map while their objectives changed. Holding territory could give way to protecting a selected player or planting explosives. Classes added different responsibilities: a medic could revive an ally, an engineer place a turret, and a tactician establish a forward spawn point. Changing orders encouraged the same streets to be reconsidered during a match, with useful positions determined by what the team needed to accomplish next.

main.title: Resident Evil 5
main.subtitle: Resident Evil Becomes a Game for Two
main.summary: Resident Evil 5 pairs Chris Redfield with Sheva Alomar in a campaign about a new biological threat.

cards.heading: Two agents enter the frame
cards.text: Resident Evil 5 pairs Chris Redfield with Sheva Alomar in a campaign about a new biological threat. Its original console release began in Japan in March 2009. The partnership makes another character a continuing presence in a series where being isolated had often been central to the tension.

cards.heading: Survival becomes shared work
cards.text: The campaign supports cooperative play. Two people must keep track of the situation and the needs of a partner, so supplies and recovery become shared concerns. The extra person can provide support, but also creates another position and another immediate problem to watch.

cards.heading: A brighter kind of danger
cards.text: Capcom used contrasts between bright light and dark interiors to shape the campaign's appearance. Sunlit locations expose Chris and Sheva as they approach threats, while darker spaces limit what they can see. This lighting accompanies the series' move towards a sustained cooperative action campaign.

main.title: Henry Hatsworth in the Puzzling Adventure
main.subtitle: An adventurer has trouble on both screens
main.summary: Henry Hatsworth in the Puzzling Adventure is EA Tiburon's Nintendo DS combination of action platforming and a block-matching puzzle game. Its gentleman explorer searches for pieces of a golden suit linked to the Puzzle Realm, with the upper screen following his physical adventure and the lower one receiving its consequences. Defeated enemies become blocks that must be dealt with below. The two games therefore share a practical problem: success in a fight does not finish the work if its remains are allowed to build into another threat on the touchscreen.

cards.heading: An adventurer has trouble on both screens
cards.text: Henry Hatsworth in the Puzzling Adventure is EA Tiburon's Nintendo DS combination of action platforming and a block-matching puzzle game. Its gentleman explorer searches for pieces of a golden suit linked to the Puzzle Realm, with the upper screen following his physical adventure and the lower one receiving its consequences. Defeated enemies become blocks that must be dealt with below. The two games therefore share a practical problem: success in a fight does not finish the work if its remains are allowed to build into another threat on the touchscreen.

cards.heading: A defeated enemy can return
cards.text: The lower grid rises as play continues, and enemy blocks reaching its upper edge can revive in Hatsworth's world. Swapping blocks into matching groups removes them and contributes energy to the Super Meter. The player has to judge when the platforming situation permits attention to move below, then clear enough space to keep the earlier victories secure. Special blocks can help or hinder the adventurer, making the puzzle board another source of immediate consequences. The connection gives matching colours a purpose beyond improving a separate score at the bottom of the display.

cards.heading: Tea Time brings something considerably larger
cards.text: Filling the Super Meter restores a younger, stronger Hatsworth, while charging it further allows Tea Time to summon a powerful robot suit. The comic transformation converts successful puzzle work into a brief advantage in the action game. Money found during the adventure can also purchase upgrades at his assistant's shop. These systems give the two halves a shared economy: enemies, energy and rewards move between them, so a well-managed puzzle can prepare the next stretch of platforming rather than merely interrupting it with an unrelated activity.

main.title: Resistance: Retribution
main.subtitle: Another soldier enters the Chimera war
main.summary: Resistance: Retribution is Bend Studio's PSP third-person shooter, first released in North America on 17 March 2009. It carries the Resistance setting into a campaign designed around the handheld, replacing the console games' first-person view with a camera behind the protagonist. The player confronts the Chimera through a portable action game whose viewpoint makes both the soldier and nearby cover visible. A familiar war becomes readable through another set of controls. The change gives Bend room to build encounters for the machine rather than reproduce a console campaign with fewer inputs.

cards.heading: Another soldier enters the Chimera war
cards.text: Resistance: Retribution is Bend Studio's PSP third-person shooter, first released in North America on 17 March 2009. It carries the Resistance setting into a campaign designed around the handheld, replacing the console games' first-person view with a camera behind the protagonist. The player confronts the Chimera through a portable action game whose viewpoint makes both the soldier and nearby cover visible. A familiar war becomes readable through another set of controls. The change gives Bend room to build encounters for the machine rather than reproduce a console campaign with fewer inputs.

cards.heading: Read the cover and the threat together
cards.text: The third-person camera places the immediate environment around the controlled character, helping the player judge where to stand and how to approach a firing position. Weapons offer different responses to the enemies encountered, encouraging attention to the situation rather than reliance on one repeated attack. The campaign links these encounters into another view of the Resistance conflict. A clear route through a fight depends on recognising what can provide protection and where the next threat is coming from, connecting movement to the use of the equipment currently available.

cards.heading: Bend gives the series a portable branch
cards.text: Christopher Reese and John Garvin directed the project, with Garvin and Jeff Ross writing and Garry Schyman composing its music. Online multiplayer originally supported eight players across modes including team battles, Capture the Flag and Assimilation. The release became the first Resistance developed outside Insomniac Games, adding another studio's handling of the setting. An emulated version reached PlayStation 4 and PlayStation 5 in 2024. Its original importance lies in that adaptation: a world introduced through console first-person shooting acquires a different camera and structure that suit a separate handheld adventure.
